questions.prompt: Write the plane through \((1,2,3)\) with normal \((2,-1,1)\).

questions.answer: Expanding gives \(2x-2-y+2+z-3=0\), so \(2x-y+z=3\).
Substitute: \(2(1)-2+3=3\). Since the equation is satisfied, the point lies on the plane.
Substitute: \(0\), which is not \(3\). So the origin is not on the plane.

questions.prompt: Find a normal vector to \(3x+4y-5z=7\).
questions.answer: The coefficients of \(x,y,z\) give a normal vector: \((3,4,-5)\).

questions.prompt: Find a plane through the origin with normal \((1,1,1)\).

questions.answer: Vectors \(B-A=(-1,1,0)\) and \(C-A=(-1,0,1)\) have cross product \((1,1,1)\). Thus \(x+y+z=1\).

questions.prompt: Find the intersection point of line \(\mathbf r=(0,0,0)+t(1,2,3)\) with plane \(x+y+z=6\).
questions.answer: Substitute: \(t+2t+3t=6\), so \(6t=6\) and \(t=1\). The point is \((1,2,3)\).

questions.prompt: Find the distance from \((1,1,1)\) to plane \(2x-y+2z=4\).
Are planes \(x+2y+3z=4\) and \(2x+4y+6z=9\) parallel?
questions.answer: Their normals \((1,2,3)\) and \((2,4,6)\) are scalar multiples, so the planes are parallel. They are distinct because doubling the first constant gives \(8\), not \(9\).

questions.prompt: Find the angle between planes with normals \((1,0,1)\) and \((0,1,1)\).
questions.answer: The angle between planes equals the angle between normals. Dot product is \(1\), magnitudes are \(\sqrt2\) and \(\sqrt2\), so the angle is \(60^\circ\).

questions.prompt: Find a parametric equation for plane \(x+y+z=1\).
Find the normal to the plane spanned by \((1,2,0)\) and \((0,1,3)\).
questions.answer: Compute the cross product: \((1,2,0)\times(0,1,3)=(6,-3,1)\).

questions.prompt: Find the plane through \((2,0,1)\) parallel to \(x-y+z=5\).
questions.answer: Parallel planes have the same normal \((1,-1,1)\). Use \((x-2)-y+(z-1)=0\), so \(x-y+z=3\).

questions.prompt: A line is given by \(\mathbf r=(1,-1,0)+t(1,2,1)\). Find where it meets the plane \(2x+3y+z=5\).
questions.answer: Substitute \(x=1+t\), \(y=-1+2t\), and \(z=t\) into the plane: \(2(1+t)+3(-1+2t)+t=5\). This simplifies to \(-1+9t=5\), so \(t=2/3\). The intersection point is \((1+2/3,-1+4/3,2/3)=(5/3,1/3,2/3)\).

questions.prompt: The line \(\mathbf r=(2,0,1)+t(1,-1,0)\) has direction parallel to the plane \(x+y+z=2\). Decide whether the whole line lies in the plane or is parallel but separate.
questions.answer: The plane normal is \((1,1,1)\), and \((1,-1,0)\cdot(1,1,1)=0\), so the direction is parallel to the plane. Test the reference point: \(2+0+1=3\), not \(2\). Since the direction is parallel but the point is not on the plane, the line is parallel to the plane but separate from it.

questions.prompt: Find the line of intersection of planes \(x+y=1\) and \(z=2\), then verify that its direction is perpendicular to both plane normals.
questions.answer: Let \(x=t\). Then \(y=1-t\) and \(z=2\), so \(\mathbf r=(0,1,2)+t(1,-1,0)\). The plane normals are \((1,1,0)\) and \((0,0,1)\). The direction \((1,-1,0)\) has dot products \(1-1+0=0\) and \(0\), so it is perpendicular to both normals.

questions.prompt: Find the plane through \(A=(1,0,2)\), \(B=(3,1,0)\), and \(C=(0,2,1)\), then test whether \(P=(2,1,1)\) lies on it.
questions.answer: Use \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(2,1,-2)\) and \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1,2,-1)\). A normal is \(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=(3,4,5)\). The plane is \(3(x-1)+4y+5(z-2)=0\), or \(3x+4y+5z=13\). For \(P=(2,1,1)\), the left side is \(6+4+5=15\), not \(13\), so \(P\) is not on the plane.

questions.prompt: Find the foot of the perpendicular from \(P=(1,2,3)\) to the plane \(2x-2y+z=6\), and give the distance from \(P\) to the plane.
questions.answer: The normal is \(\mathbf n=(2,-2,1)\). Points on the perpendicular have form \(P-\lambda\mathbf n=(1-2\lambda,2+2\lambda,3-\lambda)\). Substitute into the plane: \(2(1-2\lambda)-2(2+2\lambda)+(3-\lambda)=6\), so \(1-9\lambda=6\) and \(\lambda=-5/9\). The foot is \(P-(-5/9)\mathbf n=(19/9,8/9,32/9)\). The distance is \(|2(1)-2(2)+3-6|/|\mathbf n|=5/3\).

questions.prompt: A slab is bounded by the parallel planes \(2x-y+2z=4\) and \(2x-y+2z=10\). Find its thickness and a point on the second plane reached by moving normally from \((2,0,0)\) on the first plane.
questions.answer: The normal is \(\mathbf n=(2,-1,2)\), with magnitude \(3\). The thickness is \(|10-4|/3=2\). Moving from the first plane to the second in the normal direction requires \(\lambda\mathbf n\) with \(\mathbf n\cdot((2,0,0)+\lambda\mathbf n)=10\). Since \(\mathbf n\cdot(2,0,0)=4\) and \(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf n=9\), \(4+9\lambda=10\), so \(\lambda=2/3\). The point is \((2,0,0)+(2/3)(2,-1,2)=(10/3,-2/3,4/3)\).
